payload.title: Rust rewrite shipped object reads tenant-wide — per-record owner scoping (FR-116/234/235) not ported
payload.description:
The TS backend owner-scoped object reads (list, subscription snapshot, live
delta fan-out) per reader, relaxed by sharing grants (FR-116/FR-235), with the
writer's own echo never suppressed (FR-234). The Rust rewrite (FR-236) shipped
all three read paths as tenant-wide pass-throughs — `objects().list()` returned
every tenant row and `broadcast_to_subscribers` sent identical bytes to every
matching subscriber, with no ownership baseline or grant relaxation.

Impact: any app using object-record sharing (or per-user data) leaked
non-owned, non-granted rows to every tenant subscriber/lister over both
`GET /objects?type=` and the WS subscription. The conformance suite only
exercised the happy-path snapshot, so the gap stayed green. Discovered during
pre-merge parity review of the Rust cutover.

Fix (commit 38fd3e6): new `object_visibility` module ports the unified read
pipeline — ownership baseline (`ownerUserId` convention, fail-open for rows
with no owner value), admin bypass, writer echo, and per-record sharing-grant
relaxation gated on a cheap "any grant exists" probe. Wired into the REST list,
the WS snapshot, and the live fan-out (baseline-visible inline to preserve
synchronous delivery; owner-mismatch grantees resolved off the hot path).
Revoking/leaving a grant fans out a removal (FR-235 visibility-revoked).
`FRICK_OBJECT_VISIBILITY` (ownerScoped default | tenantWide) is the opt-out.

Tests: 6 unit + cross-user isolation on the WS snapshot, REST list, and live
fan-out, plus grant relaxation, writer echo, and visibility-revocation.
